module.purpose: Provides Content Security Policy nonce generation, request propagation, and response-header emission for web page requests.
module.summary: This module implements CSP handling across Node and Next.js request/response interfaces. It recognizes existing nonces, filters requests to page paths, generates cryptographic nonces when policy enforcement is enabled, stores them on requests, and conditionally emits a normalized CSP header on responses.
module.businessContext: Supports browser security for the web application by restricting executable and loadable resources. Failure can prevent page rendering or weaken protection against injected scripts and unauthorized resource loading.
functions: getCspPolicy (~L9-38): Builds a nonce-aware Content Security Policy string.
isPagePathRequest (~L41-46): Determines whether a URL represents a page request.
safeParseString (~L48-53): Validates unknown values before treating them as strings.
csp (~L55-111): Generates, propagates, and emits CSP nonces for requests.

env: Reads process.env.CSP_POLICY to determine whether CSP processing is enabled and whether non-strict styles are allowed.
mutationOfArg: Mutates the request x-nonce header when a page request requires CSP.
Mutates the response headers by setting Content-Security-Policy when enforcement is requested.

units.name: getCspPolicy

detail.name: getCspPolicy
preconditions: The nonce argument is provided as a string.
IS_PRODUCTION and WEBAPP_URL are available in the module scope.
postconditions: Returns a CSP policy string containing directives for default, script, object, base, child, style, font, image, and connection sources.
In production mode, the script-src directive contains the supplied nonce and strict-dynamic policy.
In non-production mode, the script-src directive permits unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, https:, and http:.
The returned img-src directive includes WEBAPP_URL.
invariants: The returned policy always contains object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none'.
The returned policy always allows app.cal.com for child-src and style-src.
The returned policy always includes 'self' for default-src, style-src, font-src, img-src, and connect-src.
edgeCases: When CSP_POLICY is exactly "non-strict", production style-src includes 'unsafe-inline'; other CSP_POLICY values do not enable this production style exception.
When IS_PRODUCTION is false, default-src includes data:, script-src includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval, and style-src includes unsafe-inline.
When IS_PRODUCTION is true, the nonce is interpolated into script-src as 'nonce-{nonce}', and style-src omits unsafe-inline unless CSP_POLICY is exactly "non-strict".
An empty nonce is interpolated without validation as 'nonce-'.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns a newline- and tab-formatted Content-Security-Policy directive string. The policy contains default-src, script-src, object-src, base-uri, child-src, style-src, font-src, img-src, and connect-src directives.
detail.summary: Builds and returns the Content Security Policy string for the current environment. The policy incorporates the supplied nonce, production mode, configured CSP policy mode, and the configured web application URL.

specLiterals.role: Exact CSP_POLICY value that enables unsafe-inline in production style-src.
Permitted inline script or style source according to environment and policy mode.

specTests.then: The result contains script-src 'nonce-abc123' 'strict-dynamic' 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:, style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' app.cal.com, and img-src 'self' https://example.com https://img.youtube.com https://eu.ui-avatars.com/api/ data:.
The result contains default-src 'self' data:, script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https: http:, and style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' app.cal.com.
The production style-src directive does not contain 'unsafe-inline', while script-src contains 'nonce-abc123' and 'strict-dynamic'.

units.name: csp

detail.name: csp
detail.signature: export function csp(req: IncomingMessage | NextRequest | null, res: OutgoingMessage | NextResponse | null)
preconditions: req may be null; when non-null it may be either an IncomingMessage or a NextRequest.
res may be null; when non-null it may be either an OutgoingMessage or a NextResponse.
For nonce generation and page-policy evaluation, req.url must be present and parseable as a URL relative to http://base_url.
postconditions: If req is null, or req.url is absent, or CSP_POLICY is disabled, or the URL is not a page-path request, the returned nonce is undefined.
If a truthy existing x-nonce header is present, it is parsed and returned without generating a new nonce or modifying the response.
For an eligible page request, a generated nonce is written to the request x-nonce header.
When a response is supplied and x-csp-enforce equals "true", the generated CSP policy is normalized and written to the response Content-Security-Policy header.
invariants: An existing truthy x-nonce header takes precedence over nonce generation and page-policy evaluation.
The generated nonce is 22 random bytes encoded by buildNonce before being used as a header value.
CSP policy whitespace runs of two or more characters are replaced with a single space and the final value is trimmed before being written.
edgeCases: A null request returns an object with nonce undefined.
A request with a truthy x-nonce header returns the parsed nonce when parsing succeeds.
A request with a truthy but invalid x-nonce header returns an empty-string nonce.
A non-null request without a URL returns an object with nonce undefined.
When CSP_POLICY is unset or otherwise falsy, no generated nonce is exposed and no CSP response header is written.
When the request URL is not a page-path request, no generated nonce is exposed and no CSP response header is written.
For an eligible page request with no response, the request nonce is set but no response header is written.
For an eligible page request whose x-csp-enforce header is not exactly "true", no response CSP header is written and the returned nonce is undefined.

raises: URL parsing errors from new URL(req.url, "http://base_url") may propagate.
Errors from nonce generation, nonce parsing, policy generation, or header operations may propagate.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Invalid existing x-nonce values are converted to an empty-string nonce; missing request or URL yields an undefined nonce.

stateMutations: Sets the request x-nonce header for eligible page requests.
Sets the response Content-Security-Policy header when enforcement is enabled.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Reads and writes x-nonce and x-csp-enforce request headers. When enforced, writes a normalized CSP policy to the Content-Security-Policy response header.
detail.summary: Determines whether a request should receive a CSP nonce and, when enforcement is enabled, applies the generated nonce and CSP policy to the request and response headers. Existing request nonces are reused after validation.
